title: How Much a Stock Market Fall Would Reduce GDP Growth Over the Next Year
units: Percentage points of GDP growth over the next year
source: Federal Reserve Board (Financial Accounts, FRB/US); Bureau of Economic Analysis; author’s calculations.
note: Fall in the stock market from its 2026 level. FRB/US: the Board’s model as run in the Econvitals Macroeconomic Simulator, including the Fed’s response, imports and every other channel in the model; the lower-earnings version moves only household wealth, the higher-return version also raises businesses’ cost of capital. The 1-cent and 3-cent columns take the whole cut in annual spending off growth in the first year. The historical consumption function (2.2 cents per dollar, estimated on 1955–2019) phases in at its estimated pace, about 72 percent within a year. None of the last three has a response from the Fed or an allowance for imports. Bold: the author’s preferred case.
columns: Historical consumption function (2 cents per dollar)
